text:
maya: quick lunchtime debate — if the office toaster was an LLM, which model would it be? :toast:
liam: obviously a stubborn but reliable older model. always fries your bread but somehow verbose on settings :sweat_smile:
devon: toaster = 1-parameter model: temperature. it only understands `TOAST_LEVEL` 😂
ash: I vote for 'Llama-crumbs' — smaller, cheerful, gets confused by bagels but fast.
kelly: gpt-4o-toaster: apologizes for burning your toast, writes a 3-paragraph apology email to the bread, offers a coupon. :crying_face:
ryan: ops-bot: "Toaster v1.0: latency 2s, throughput 2 slices/min, known issue: occasionally launches small smoke signals." :robot_face:
maya: steal this for lunch poll? quick reaction emoji vote. :thumbsup: for nostalgia-toaster (old but consistent), :fire: for drama-toaster (burns sometimes but hotter), :clap: for apologetic-llm-toaster
liam: :thumbsup:
devon: :fire:
kelly: :clap: lol
ash: thinking about prompt engineering: `Make toast crisp but not incandescent.` somehow always ends up with charcoal.
maya: someone should write a unit test: `assert(toast.level == 'golden')` — flaky in prod. :joy:
ryan: can we get a toaster dashboard in the kitchen? toast latency, crumb cache hit-rate, #burns today. I'd monitor that.
liam: naming suggestion: 'Redwood Crisp' — sounds like a startup toaster.
maya: OK that's our team name for the potluck theme. thanks everyone, I'll make a tiny poll in #random for real votes. :tada:
ops-bot: deploy reminder — kitchen router reboot scheduled at 3pm, toaster may be unavailable for ~2 minutes. :bell:
